stem:
Xavier has a paper heart and a possible vertical mid-line drawn on it.

When is that mid-line a line of symmetry?

options.text: Whenever the heart looks roughly balanced, even if it is never folded.
When folding along the mid-line is treated as a result produced by an already known line of symmetry.
Only when folding along that mid-line makes the two parts overlap exactly point for point.
Only when a group-theory symmetry order of 2 is named for the heart.

teacher.key_rationale: A line of symmetry requires the fold-overlap test: the two parts must match exactly point for point along that line.
